newsitem.title: FRANCE: Council of Europe urges stricter rules on cloning.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe urges stricter rules on cloning.

text.p: The head of the Council of Europe, which safeguards democracy and human rights, called on Tuesday for stricter bioethics regulations to prevent any human cloning.

Council secretary-general Daniel Tarschys said the prospect of human clones was "unacceptable" after British scientists who cloned the sheep Dolly, the first animal to be succesfully cloned from an adult cell, prompted widespread concern.
"The cloning of an adult sheep is without doubt an impressive scientific achievement, but it shows that stricter bioethics rules are necessary," he said in a statement.
Tarschys noted that the Council's 40 members had recently agreed on a human rights and biomedicine convention, the first international text governing bioethics.
